subsystems.name: Expert networks
subsystems.role: specialised sub-networks, usually feed-forward layers, that process only the tokens routed to them.

subsystems.name: Gating network (router)
subsystems.role: scores each token for every expert and selects the top-k experts to activate.

subsystems.name: Token dispatch and combination
subsystems.role: moves tokens to the selected experts and merges their outputs weighted by the gate scores.

subsystems.name: Load balancing and auxiliary losses
subsystems.role: encourages even expert usage so that a few experts do not dominate or collapse.

subsystems.name: Expert parallelism and communication
subsystems.role: distributes experts across devices and coordinates token exchange between them.

subsystems.name: Training and inference orchestration
subsystems.role: manages the conditional computation pipeline, batching, and scheduling.

buildSteps.title: Choose MoE placement
buildSteps.detail: Decide which layers to replace with a mixture of experts, typically every other feed-forward layer, and set the number of experts and how many are active per token (top-k).

buildSteps.title: Implement the gating network
buildSteps.detail: Add a small linear layer that outputs a score for each expert per token, apply softmax, and select the top-k experts.

buildSteps.title: Set capacity factor
buildSteps.detail: Define a maximum number of tokens each expert can process per batch to bound compute; tokens beyond capacity are dropped or passed through a residual path.

buildSteps.title: Add auxiliary losses
buildSteps.detail: Introduce a load balancing loss to encourage uniform expert usage and a router z-loss to stabilise training.

buildSteps.title: Distribute experts
buildSteps.detail: Shard experts across accelerators and implement all-to-all communication so tokens can reach their assigned experts.

buildSteps.title: Train with conditional computation
buildSteps.detail: In the forward pass, route tokens, compute only the selected experts, and combine their outputs; in the backward pass, update only those experts and the router.

buildSteps.title: Tune routing and capacity
buildSteps.detail: Adjust top-k, capacity factor, and the weight of the load balancing loss to balance model quality against throughput.

buildSteps.title: Deploy for inference
buildSteps.detail: Optimise kernels for sparse activation, handle dynamic batching, and perform expert selection on the fly with minimal latency.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Watch for expert collapse or underutilisation, then retrain or adjust the load balancing scheme as needed.

prerequisites.why: Training many experts requires sharding both model and data across many accelerators.
All-to-all communication between experts is bandwidth-intensive and can bottleneck training.

prerequisites.tech: Sparse tensor operations and efficient kernels
prerequisites.why: Conditional computation relies on fast gather, scatter, and grouped matrix multiplications.
Without them, a few experts receive most tokens, wasting capacity and degrading quality.
Expert parallelism is a form of model parallelism that must be orchestrated alongside data parallelism.

pathway.milestone: Very large language models use MoE to scale parameters without a proportional increase in compute.
pathway.unlocks: Cheaper scaling of model capacity for training and inference.

pathway.milestone: Improved routing algorithms that reduce token dropping and encourage better expert specialisation.
pathway.unlocks: Higher quality per unit of compute and more stable training.

pathway.milestone: Hardware and software co-design for all-to-all communication.
pathway.unlocks: Faster training and inference, enabling more experts and larger models.

pathway.milestone: Conditional computation beyond MoE, such as adaptive depth and width per token.
pathway.unlocks: Models that spend compute only where needed, further improving efficiency.
